Standard: The engine is free of damaging vibration, damaging resonance conditions, or other damaging DR, regardless of propulsion system excitation source, when operated, at all engine-rotational speeds and thrust or power settings under installed or uninstalled steady state and transient conditions, at maximum allowable field imbalance of the engine rotor systems, IAW 7.3.1 for the stated life documented in engine technical data. a. Maximum engine mechanical vibration limits, for both installed and uninstalled operation, are defined for each measurement location and direction as functions of frequency, and engine order. b. Damaging critical speeds for engine rotor systems or rotating assemblies do not occur in the rotor speed range from 20% below idle speed to 20% above maximum operating speed. Damping and balancing allow any critical speed that exists from rotor rest to 20% above maximum operating speed to be traversed with smooth engine operation and without engine damage. c. The natural frequencies of the mounting system with the engine installed are at least 20% below idle shaft rotational speed(s) in all damaging modes of vibration which can be excited by rotor imbalance. d. Windmilling operation does not result in damaging vibration to the engine or air vehicle. Windmilling following a blade out event does not result in any condition not allowed under the 7.3.12 standard. e. All rotor areas that could puddle oil incorporate drains to limit potential imbalance. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Rotating component and rotating assembly, balance limits and procedures are defined for production and sustainment in engine technical data.
(2) Engine vibration limits are defined in engine technical data.
(3) Review of product definition data and models verifies that rotor oil drain features are present. Analysis.
  (1) Analysis is accomplished to determine vibratory characteristics of the complete engine system installed in the air vehicle. A dynamic model of the total engine system including all relevant mass, stiffness, damping, and boundary conditions (e.g., rotor(s), bearings, supports, dampers, frames, cases, mounts, air vehicle interface) is developed to analyze critical speeds and associated DRs. Analysis and models are calibrated to engine test results. Calibrated models are used to evaluate sensitivity to influence parameters (e.g., boundary conditions, imbalance distribution and phase, thermal bow, misalignment, operating conditions).
  (2) Analysis is accomplished to determine the range of windmilling speeds, considering installation effects, for each rotor throughout the engine operating envelope. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Resonance search testing (ping testing) is accomplished on fully assembled and instrumented ground test engine.
    (2) Lab test: Instrumented engine testing is accomplished in sea level and altitude test cells to verify critical speed predictions, imbalance sensitivity, case deflections, and vibration amplitude. The full engine speed range up to 105% scheduled physical speed is tested. Start tests examine sub-idle operation and effects of bowed rotor. Effects of rotor imbalance up to the maximum allowable field limit, using worst-case phase and mass placement as determined by analysis of imbalance sensitivity, are verified by test.
    (3) Lab test: Full engine durability test or AMT/ASMET is conducted in a ground-based sea level test cell IAW JSSG-2007, Appendix A, Verification section, Endurance Tests paragraph. Tests include product-representative inlet conditions and extractions, and rotor imbalance. Tests are conducted using engine control software or schedules of the type design. Post-test teardown inspection of hardware is accomplished to document condition. Minimum endurance test duration is twice the planned flight test duration. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
    (4) Lab test: Full engine durability test or AMT/ASMET is conducted in a ground-based sea level test cell IAW JSSG-2007, Appendix A, Verification section, Endurance Tests paragraph. Tests include product-representative inlet conditions and extractions, and rotor imbalance. Tests are conducted using engine control software or schedules of the type design. Post-test teardown inspection of hardware is accomplished to document condition. Minimum endurance test duration is the scheduled depot inspection interval or half the cold part DSL.
    (5) Flight test: Vibration testing with an instrumented engine is conducted to verify installed vibratory environment and response.
